news.headline: STAT News Previews uniQure's Still-Pending Four-Year AMT-130 Readout
news.summary: STAT confirms the closely-watched four-year Phase I/II data (24 patients across both dose cohorts) has still not been released and remains guided for before the end of September 2026, following three-year data that showed a 75% slowing of disease progression in the high-dose group.

news.headline: Sell-side consensus firms at Moderate Buy with $65 average price target across 17 brokerages
news.summary: A compiled ratings snapshot shows seventeen brokerages covering uniQure at a consensus "Moderate Buy," with fourteen buy ratings, two holds and one sell, and an average twelve-month price objective of $65.00. The reading reflects post-BLA-filing sell-side sentiment settling roughly 30-45% above the stock's early-September trading range.

news.headline: uniQure submits US BLA and UK MAA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, requests Priority Review
news.summary: uniQure filed a Biologics License Application with the FDA seeking accelerated approval for ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130) and, in parallel, a Marketing Authorisation Application with the UK MHRA, both supported by the three-year Phase I/II analysis versus a propensity-score-matched Enroll-HD external control. The company requested priority review, which would compress the FDA review to roughly six months, and reiterated plans to present four-year Phase I/II data before the end of Q3 2026.

news.headline: William Blair Resumes Coverage at Outperform with $73 Value as the Stock Round-Trips the Filing Pop
news.summary: Analyst Sami Corwin resumed coverage with an Outperform rating and a $73 sum-of-the-parts value, calling FDA acceptance of the BLA the next incremental de-risking event and approval itself the substantial one; William Blair models peak global AMT-130 sales of about $3.2B in 2035. Shares nonetheless sold the news, spiking to an intraday $50.74 on September 3 before closing back near $45.

news.headline: ICER Opens a Cost-Effectiveness Review of AMT-130 with a March 2027 CEPAC Meeting
news.summary: The Institute for Clinical and Economic Review launched an assessment of AMT-130, with public comment on the draft scoping document open until September 11, 2026. The Midwest CEPAC will publicly deliberate and vote on the evidence in March 2027, making this the first formal US payer-value review of the therapy.

news.headline: RTW Investments and Susquehanna Disclose New Stakes in uniQure in 13G Filings
news.summary: RTW Investments reported a beneficial stake of roughly 3.94M shares (about 5.7%) and Susquehanna-affiliated entities disclosed a 3.34M-share (4.8%) position in filings accepted by the SEC on August 14. The disclosures pointed to continued institutional accumulation ahead of the BLA submission and the four-year AMT-130 data.

catalysts.label: Four-year AMT-130 Phase I/II data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure has committed to presenting the four-year Phase I/II analysis before the end of Q3 2026, and a September 10 STAT News preview confirmed it remains pending. The dataset covers all 24 patients from the first two cohorts (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose) at four years plus additional high-dose patients at three years, benchmarked against the Enroll-HD natural-history database. With the BLA already filed, this is the single biggest near-term swing factor for the stock, and it can land on any trading day before quarter-end.

catalysts.label: ICER revised scoping document
catalysts.detail: ICER's public comment period on the draft scoping document for its AMT-130 review closed September 11, 2026; a revised scoping document is expected on or about September 21. The framing set here shapes the value benchmark US payers will use against uniQure's eventual price for a one-time gene therapy, ahead of the January 2027 draft evidence report and March 2027 CEPAC vote.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 second-cohort enrollment completion
catalysts.detail: uniQure guided at Q2 results to completing enrollment of the second, higher-dose cohort (six patients) in the Phase I/IIa refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy study during Q3 2026, so confirmation is due by September 30.

catalysts.label: FDA filing decision and priority review determination
catalysts.detail: The FDA has a 60-day filing review period on the BLA submitted September 2, so acceptance for review should be communicated around early November 2026. The same decision point reveals whether priority review was granted - the difference between a six-month and a ten-month review clock, and therefore between an accelerated-approval action date around late April/early May 2027 versus late 2027.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 results and regulatory update
catalysts.detail: uniQure's Q3 2026 print is expected around early-to-mid November 2026 per consensus earnings-calendar estimates, not yet formally confirmed by the company. It is the first scheduled opportunity for management to confirm BLA acceptance, the review designation and PDUFA date, and progress on the UK MAA against the roughly $810M cash position that funds operations into 2030.

catalysts.label: FDA advisory committee (AdCom) decision
catalysts.detail: Management has said an advisory committee meeting for what would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease is probable and the company is preparing for one. The FDA has not confirmed a meeting or a date; timing would follow BLA acceptance rather than submission.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory trial initiation
catalysts.detail: uniQure and the FDA have aligned on the key design elements of the required confirmatory study: roughly 200 patients randomized 2:1 to AMT-130 versus standard of care, with Total Functional Capacity at 36 months as the primary endpoint. Enrollment is expected to be underway before the FDA's accelerated-approval decision.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 higher-dose epilepsy data and AMT-191 Fabry update
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans updated Phase I/IIa data in refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy in H1 2027, including the second, higher-dose cohort, plus a Fabry (AMT-191) update; dosing there remains paused pending evaluation of liver enzyme elevations in two mid-dose patients.

catalysts.label: ICER evidence report and CEPAC verdict
catalysts.detail: ICER's draft evidence report on AMT-130 is due in January 2027, followed by a Midwest CEPAC public meeting in March 2027 where the panel deliberates and votes, and a final report in April 2027 - landing essentially on top of the expected FDA action date.

catalysts.label: Potential FDA accelerated approval decision for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: With priority review granted, the FDA action date would land around late April or early May 2027, making AMT-130 potentially the first approved disease-modifying therapy for Huntington's disease. Without priority review the decision slips toward late 2027.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing authorisation decision
catalysts.detail: The MAA filed with the MHRA on September 2 runs on its own clock, independent of the FDA. William Blair expects approval in both countries during 2027, but uniQure has not disclosed an expected MHRA decision timeline.

pulse: As of September 12, uniQure's headline catalyst - the four-year AMT-130 data - still has not been released, even though the company already filed its US BLA and UK MAA on three-year data back on September 2; a September 10 STAT News piece reconfirmed the readout remains pending and guided for before quarter-end, and no further update has emerged since. Sentiment stays broadly bullish but nervy while the market waits: William Blair resumed at Outperform ($73 target) on September 2, and a September 8 consensus read showed 14 of 17 covering brokerages at buy with an average $65 price target, with no new insider selling, financing or negative regulatory news since the filing. ICER's scoping-comment window closed September 11 with a revised document due around September 21, and attention otherwise sits on the still-undated four-year data due before September 30 and the FDA's filing/priority-review decision expected around early November, with Q3 earnings shortly after.
